# Introduction
\vspace{-6mm}

For Aim 1, we will be testing the hypothesis that memory consolidation and AD-signature corticol thickness can be predicted by higher baseline cytokine and chemokine levels.
We will also assess whether decreases in episodic memory and corticol thickness over a one year period are associated with increases in cytokine and chemokine levels.

# Methods

\vspace{-8mm}
## Data Analysis
\vspace{-6mm}

For these analyses, we will use general multiple linear regression models for each outcome of interest. 
For both Aim 1 and Aim 2, 
the primary outcomes of interest consist of the 5 memory consolidation variables as well as gray matter corticol thickness.
The primary explanatory variables (PEVs) of interest are the 4 chemokine/cytokine variables: IL-6, TNF-$\alpha$, MCD-1, and Eotaxin-1. 
We will adjust for age and sex in these models with additional covariates as necessary. 

For Aim 1a, we will use a general linear model for each of the 6 primary outcomes.
For each model, the outcome will be the value of the outcome at Year 1 and we will adjust for baseline values of the outcome as well as baseline values of the 4 chemokine/cytokine variables. 
This model will allow us to determine if increases in baseline levels of the chemokine/cytokine markers are associated with changes in memory consolidation or corticol thickness after 1 year.
<!-- Memory consolidation in this case is Long Term Consoidation I believe! -->
For Aim 1b, we will also use general linear regression where the outcome will be the given outcome of interest at year 1. 
We will adjust for baseline levels of the outcome as well as baseline levels of both chemokines and cytokines. The PEVs will be the difference in Year 1 from baseline for each of the four chemokines/cytokines. 
These particular variables will allow us to determine whether greater increases in the chemokines/cytokines are associated with greater declines in episodic memory and corticol thickness.
For Aim 2, the model will be exactly as the model used for Aim 1b with the difference that we will additinally include baseline levels of Amyloid deposition as well as an interaction between the change in Amyloid Deposition from Year 1 to baseline with the change in the chemokine/cytokine levels from Year 1 to baseline. 
We will create 4 models for the each of the 4 possible chemokine/cytokine variables with the amyloid deposition variable. 
These interactions will allow us to determine if the change in Amyloid Deposition with memory consolidtion/AD-corticol thickness differs depending on the levels of chemokine/cytokine levels. 

We will additionally adjust for education, cardiovascular markers, 
<!-- (BMI, blood pressure, history of hypercholesterolemia),  -->
immune health history variables,
Clinical Dementia Rating, Geriartric Depression Scale, use of Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory drugs, 
<!-- (recent infections and illnesses, surgical procedures in the past year, and auto-immune conditions),  -->
routinely collected cognitive measures,
<!-- (MoCA and neuropsychological assessment), -->
and APOE genotype as necessary.
Because the potential number of covariates is quite large, we will assess the relationships that the variables have with each other to determine if two variables are strongly correlated to reduce the number of covariates. 
<!-- Correlation matrix -->
We will check if any variables are associated with both the outcome and the primary explanatory variable, also known as a confounder.
Lastly, we will check if precision variables exist which are variables that are only associated with the outcome and not the PEV. 
Including precision variables will allow us to get more precise estimates of the exposure-outcome association.
With the remaining variables, we will conduct iterative Partial-F-Tests to assess if a reduction of these variables results in a more simple and parismonious model.
